chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from one of his companions, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ismail ibn Abi Qurrat, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When a man dies, what is for him and what is against him, from the debt, is released/freed.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's debts when they die according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the phrase 'his debt is freed' (ḥalla) signifies that the personal liability of the deceased is extinguished, transferring the obligation to their estate (turath) for settlement before inheritance distribution. This ruling underscores the priority of creditors' rights in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that financial dues are cleared from the deceased's account prior to the allocation of shares to heirs, thereby maintaining social and economic justice.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from one of his companions, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Ismail Bin Abu Qurrat, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘When the man dies, it frees up what is for him and what is against him, from the debts’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from certain persons of his people from Khalaf ibn Hammad from ‘Isma’il ibn abu Qurrah from abu Basir who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When a man dies, payment of all of loans for and against him opens up (becomes due). 5 ”
